newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down on RBI dollar purchases.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down on RBI dollar purchases.

text.p: The Indian rupee recovered slightly in afternoon trade to end Monday at 35.780/785 per dollar, off the day's low of 35.80 but well below the opening quotes of 35.745/755, dealers said.
Dealers said the rupee traded at a high of 35.75 and a low of 35.80 on Monday.
Sustained spot dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) pushed the rupee down, taking the market by surprise, dealers said.
"We were anticipating another quiet day of range-bound trade," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The RBI took us by surprise."

"Given their (RBI's) somewhat ambivalent attitude in recent times, no-one was really expecting the RBI to hit the market the way it did today," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "At a conservative estimate, we think they must have bought around $150 million today."
Dealers said the RBI bought dollars several times during the day, starting around the 35.75 level up to 35.80.
"Possibly the fact that the rupee opened down against the forward dollar might have prompted the RBI intervention in the spot market," said another dealer.
"This way there is combined pressure on the rupee and the scale of intervention need not be very large," he said.
Exporters have been complaining the rupee is overvalued by around 7.0-8.0 percent against the dollar and want a fall in its value to help them maintain their competitiveness.
RBI intervention to stem the rupee's rise has been limited recently by worriews it may lead to over expanasion of the domestic money supply.
The Indian rupee opened Monday down against the forward dollar on higher call money rates and fears of tightening domestic liquidity, dealers said.
"With the cost of funding going up, forward premiums rose in tandem," said a dealer.
Indian call money was traded in a 9.5-10.5 percent range for most of Monday and ended at 8.75-9.75, dealers said.
Call money was below 1.0 percent for most of April but government bond issues have drained liquidity and helped rates firm.
Dealers said the annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Monday at 5.31 percent against the weekend close of 4.65 but some dealers felt there was little chance of further rise.
"Basically even today, there was not much movement," said a dealer. "Premiums opened up on higher call money rates. But there was not really much movement after that."
"Call should soon ease to around 6.0-7.0 percent," the dealer said. "There is therefore little risk of forwards rising further unless importers rush in to cover forward exposures."
